title: Multi-Detailed 3D Architectural Framework for Sound Perception Research in Virtual Reality
central_proposition: This paper proposes a comprehensive, multi-detailed 3D architectural framework for sound perception research in virtual reality, integrating visual and acoustic cues across three levels of detail to bridge the gap between architectural modeling practices and specific research demands.

concept_definitions.name: Modeler
concept_definitions.definition: The person concerned with the task of 3D preparation workflow for research demands.

concept_definitions.name: Virtual Acoustic Environments (VAEs)
concept_definitions.definition: Simulation environments with full control over virtual sound sources, playing back definable source signals.

concept_definitions.name: Auralization
concept_definitions.definition: The process of simulating auditory environments, including sound generation, sound transmission, signal processing, and sound reproduction.

concept_definitions.name: Building Information Modeling (BIM)
concept_definitions.definition: An object-oriented CAD system providing a single logical, consistent source for all information associated with a building, integrating geometrical data with additional non-graphic attributes.

concept_definitions.name: Levels of Detail (LoD)
concept_definitions.definition: Categorization of visual and acoustic cues (geometry, materials, lighting, viewers, sound sources, listeners) into low, medium, and high complexity levels for modeling.

argument_structure: The paper identifies a gap between architectural 3D modeling and sound perception research needs in VR. It reviews existing simulation prerequisites and software for both visual and acoustic domains. Based on this, it proposes a structured, modular framework with three levels of detail for various cues. The framework's application is demonstrated with two case studies, and its implications for transparency and future cross-modality approaches are discussed.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The framework's core mechanism is the structured decomposition of complex 3D modeling tasks into modular, interconnected components (visual/acoustic cues, levels of detail). This modularity facilitates interdisciplinary communication, allows for flexible customization to specific experimental needs, optimizes computational efficiency by enabling detail simplification, and enhances reproducibility through standardized module definitions. By aligning with architectural modeling traditions, it aims to improve usability and ecological validity for perception studies.

findings.antecedent: Lack of knowledge overlap between architectural 3D modeling and sound perception research demands in VR
findings.consequent: Gap between architect's deliverable and contextual scenario for overarching research purposes
findings.mechanism: Building modelers often lack diverse knowledge (sound sources, propagation models, material models) required for sound perception research, leading to simplified models or inefficient collaboration.
findings.quote: there is still a gap between the architect's deliverable and the contextual scenario for overarching research purposes, mainly caused by the lack of knowledge in the areas where research disciplines overlap.

findings.antecedent: Application of a multi-detailed 3D architectural framework (visual and acoustic cues, three levels of detail)
findings.consequent: Coverage of very specific research application needs and modularity for future modeling demands
findings.mechanism: The framework's modularity and defined levels of detail allow researchers to select and combine components precisely tailored to their experimental requirements, optimizing for plausibility and computational effort.
findings.quote: this article presents a comprehensive framework, defined by the visual and acoustic cues... on one side and three levels of detail on the other. In this way, very specific research application needs can be covered, as well as a modular concept for future modeling demands.

findings.antecedent: Interconnection between every model element in the proposed framework
findings.consequent: Assembly among different modalities at different levels of detail
findings.mechanism: Explicit design of interconnections ensures compatibility and seamless integration of visual and acoustic components, even when different levels of detail are chosen for each modality.
findings.quote: The interconnection between every model element is particularly designed, enabling the assembly among different modalities at different levels of detail.

findings.consequent: More adequate framework for comprehensive visual and acoustic models
findings.mechanism: Aligning the framework with architects' common object-based modeling techniques and separating geometry from material definitions (as opposed to acoustic simulation's combined approach) makes it more intuitive and usable for modelers.
findings.quote: Since the architectural modeling is often object based... the separation between geometry and material definitions seems more adequate for an architectural framework.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Schröder, 2011 (acoustic simulation combines geometry and material)

findings.antecedent: Use of the proposed multi-detailed 3D architectural framework
findings.consequent: Transparency in definitions and interpretations of both visual and auditory aspects, and potential for future cross-modality approaches in architectural acoustics
findings.mechanism: The structured categorization schemes (Table 2) provide clear, standardized definitions for visual and acoustic cues at different levels of detail, reducing ambiguity and facilitating interdisciplinary collaboration and the development of integrated models.
findings.quote: The categorization schemes as listed in Table 2 may achieve transparency in terms of the definitions and interpretations of both visual and auditory aspects, and possibly in the future, the development of a cross-modality approaches to modeling in architectural acoustics.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: The proposed framework will reduce the time and effort required for 3D modeling for sound perception research in VR compared to ad-hoc methods.
Researchers using the framework will report higher satisfaction with the quality and relevance of 3D models for their specific experimental needs.
The modularity of the framework will enable easier integration of new modeling techniques or software tools in the future.
The framework will facilitate interdisciplinary collaboration between architects and acoustics researchers by providing a common, structured language for model specification.
Virtual environments created using the framework will demonstrate high ecological validity for sound perception studies, comparable to real-world measurements or recordings.
bridge_warrants: The framework explicitly connects architectural modeling (CAD, BIM) with virtual acoustics (Auralization) and computer graphics (rendering, animation).
It addresses the need for multisensory integration (visual and acoustic cues) in VR environments for perception research.
It implicitly supports theories of cognitive load by allowing optimization of detail levels, thus potentially reducing unnecessary processing.
methodological_critiques: Current architectural 3D modelers often use simulation techniques without a deep theoretical understanding, relying on them as feedback tools rather than grounded analyses.
There is a lack of research on automatic simplification of CAD models to an acoustically relevant resolution.

Achieving perfect ecological validity in simulations is challenging; 'blind input data quality and modeling quality determine the uncertainties of the auditory impression at the end,' highlighting the need for robust material characterization.
model_structure: The framework is presented as a double-entry table (Table 1) with 'Cues' (Visual: Geometries, Materials, Lighting, Viewers; Acoustic: Geometries, Materials, Sound sources, Listeners) on the vertical axis and 'Level of detail' (Low, Medium, High) on the horizontal axis. Each cell defines a specific module (e.g., 'Visual Geometries Low: Sphere'). The framework emphasizes the interconnection and modular assembly of these elements.
limitations: The framework is conceptual and not tied to specific proprietary software tools, implying that the choice of tools can vary.
While the framework provides structure, the ultimate quality and fine details of the model depend on the modeler's execution within each module.
The framework intentionally excludes artistic postprocessing techniques (e.g., image tinting, spectral correction) to maintain controlled values for laboratory conditions.
The accuracy of auditory impressions in simulations is limited by the quality of input data and modeling, particularly for acoustic material properties.

paper_metadata.title: Multi-Detailed 3D Architectural Framework for Sound Perception Research in Virtual Reality
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Multi-Detailed 3D Architectural Framework for Sound Perception Research in Virtual Reality
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: The presentation of architectural design in simulation environments demands strong 3D modeling abilities. Architects usually demonstrate presentation skills that mostly address researchers in the building simulation field. However, there is still a gap between the architect’s deliverable and the contextual scenario for overarching research purposes, mainly caused by the lack of knowledge in the areas where research disciplines overlap. This dilemma is particularly present in the practice of 3D modeling for sound perception research in virtual reality since the building modelers must also gather diverse pieces of knowledge into a contained scenario: ranging from sound sources, sound propagation models to physically based material models. Grounded on this need, this article presents a comprehensive framework, defined by the visual and acoustic cues—geometries, materials, sources, receivers, and postprocessing—on one side and three levels of detail on the other. In this way, very specific research application needs can be covered, as well as a modular concept for future modeling demands. The interconnection between every model element is particularly designed, enabling the assembly among different modalities at different levels of detail. Finally, it provides targeted modeling strategies for architects, depicted in one indoor and one outdoor demonstration for auditory-visual research.
